This can cause the abrasion of the wiring itself. This abrasion may cause a short-circuit and consequent inadvertent deployment of the steering wheel airbag.
jeep.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to inspect the airbag wiring and apply cut proof padded tape.

jeep.defect: CAMSHAFT MAY FAIL Due to an error in the production process the engine camshaft may break.
jeep.remedy: Check affected vehicles and where necessary replace the camshaft.

jeep.defect: BRAKE VACUUM ASSISTANCE MAY REDUCE In some cases due to the non-compliance of the engine ECU software the engine failure warning lamp may illuminate. As a consequence the vacuum assistance available to the braking system may be reduced.
jeep.remedy: Recall affected vehicles and re-programme the engine ECU with updated software.

jeep.defect: THE SPORT MODE SYSTEM MAY NOT BE SET CORRECTLY AND THEREFORE MAY NOT COMPLY WITH TYPE APPROVAL REQUIREMENTS The �Sport� mode system may not be set correctly and therefore may not comply with type approval requirements.
jeep.remedy: The proxi file must be updated to solve the non conformity.

jeep.defect: VEHICLE MAY ROLL AWAY The electronic shift lever on about 210000 of the above vehicles may allow a roll away condition if the vehicle�s engine is left running the parking brake is not engaged and the transmission is not in the �PARK� position before exiting the vehicle.
jeep.remedy: On affected vehicles new software will be installed which includes an �Auto Park� feature. A handbook addendum leaflet will also be provided.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF VEHICLE SAFETY FEATURES The ignition switch may unintentionally change position while driving.  This may result in a loss of engine power power steering assist power brake assist or disable the airbag function.
jeep.remedy: On affected vehicles replace the ignition switch and lock cylinder

jeep.defect: FIRE MAY OCCUR The sun visors may experience a high resistance short at the sun visor vanity lamp wiring after a service repair to the sun visor headliner or while gaining access above the headliner. This may result in an inoperative vanity lamp and/or an electrical fire.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the sun visors modify the surrounding sheet metal and install vanity lamp wiring guides.

jeep.defect: VEHICLE MAY ROLL AWAY The automatic transmission may shift into or through neutral unintentionally when parked which in some circumstances could allow the vehicle to move/runaway.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to attach a software update to remove possibility of inadvertent shifting.

jeep.defect: INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR VEHICLE LIGHTING MAY FAIL It is possible under extreme conditions that the wiring harness under the dashboard could come into contact with the steering column. This over a period of time may result in the chaffing of wires in the harness. If this should occur then it is possible both the exterior and instrument lights could fail.
jeep.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to provide additional security of the wiring loom.

jeep.defect: FRONT SEAT SHOULDER BELTS ADJUSTABLE ANCHORS MAY HAVE INADEQUATE STRENGTH The front shoulder belt adjustable anchors on affected vehicles may have been improperly manufactured and could have inadequate strength. An anchor with inadequate strength may allow the front shoulder belt to separate from the anchor under certain accident conditions.
jeep.remedy: To correct this condition both front shoulder belt adjustable anchors must be replaced.

jeep.defect: INDICATORS MAY NOT FUNCTION CORRECTLY The bulb failure detection system may not alert the driver to the failure of a rear indicator bulb.
jeep.remedy: Reprogram the Body control Module with new software.

jeep.defect: BRAKING EFFICIENCY MAY BE REDUCED A connector on the brake servo pipe may fail and cause a loss of vacuum assistance necessitating the driver to include additional effort when braking.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to fit a new brake servo pipe.

jeep.defect: INCORRECT SPARE WHEEL Some vehicles with alloy wheels may have been supplied with an unsuitable space saver spare wheel. If fitted this spare wheel could cause interference with braking system components.
jeep.remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace any unsuitable spare wheels with correctly specified versions.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE CRACKING OF LOWER ENGINE STABILISER ROD The lower engine stabiliser rod may crack or break. This could result in detachment of the off side drive shaft on full lock.
jeep.remedy: Inspect the stabiliser rod welding and fit a new rod where found necessary.

jeep.defect: THE FUEL SUPPLY LINE CONNECTOR MAY CRACK The fuel supply line connector may crack.
jeep.remedy: Inspect the date code on the fuel line tag. If the date falls within the specified range replace the line. If the tag is missing replace the line.

jeep.defect: FRONT BRAKE ROTORS (DISCS) MAY FAIL. There is a possibility that corrosion may cause the front brake rotors (Discs) to separate from the centre hub section. Vehicle may pull to one side when braking. Also braking efficiency will be reduced.
jeep.remedy: Recall affected vehicles for inspection and if necessary replacement of both front brake rotors with new version. ( Note. Some vehicles will already have the new version fitted)

jeep.defect: On affected vehicles the rear coil springs may not have been installed correctly which may lead to one or both of them detaching from the vehicle while driving. On affected vehicles the rear coil springs may not have been installed correctly which may lead to one or both of them detaching from the vehicle while driving.
jeep.remedy: Inspect installation of both rear coil springs and if necessary remove and refit correctly.

jeep.defect: On certain vehicles equipped with an Air Conditioning compressor these may experience the condition of a powertrain shutdown in the event of an AC compressor issue. This could result in the engine non-starting or stalling. On certain vehicles equipped with an Air Conditioning compressor these may experience the condition of a powertrain shutdown in the event of an AC compressor issue. This could result in the engine non-starting or stalling.
jeep.remedy: The repair is an upload of modified ECU software.

jeep.defect: THE BODY CONTROL MODULE SOFTWARE MAY ALLOW THE ENGINE STOP START SYSTEM TO OPERATE OUTSIDE OF THE EMISSIONS CERTIFICATION The body control module software may allow engine stop start behaviour that was not part of the emissions certification.
jeep.remedy: Update the body control module software.

jeep.defect: FRACTURE OF FRONT COIL SPRINGS The anti noise plastic shields fitted to the bottom of the front suspension coil springs may permit the accumulation of a high level of humidity under certain environmental conditions. When combined with the presence of salt and small stones etc. this condition may cause breakage of the spring(s) and subsequent tearing of the tyre as a result of the fractured coils contacting the tyre wall.
jeep.remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for the fitment of a modified ventilated spring sheath and inspection of the front coil springs.

jeep.defect: On certain vehicles equipped with an Air Conditioning compressor these may experience the condition of a powertrain shutdown in the event of an AC compressor issue. This could result in the engine non-starting or stalling. On certain vehicles equipped with an Air Conditioning compressor these may experience the condition of a powertrain shutdown in the event of an AC compressor issue. This could result in the engine non-starting or stalling.
jeep.remedy: The repair is an upload of modified ECU software.

jeep.defect: THE PASSENGER AIRBAG (PAB) MAY CONTAIN LOOSE FASTNERS DUE TO AN ASSEMBLY PROBLEM AT THE SUPPLIER The Passenger Airbag (PAB) may contain loose fasteners.
jeep.remedy: Replace passenger airbag.

jeep.defect: BRAKING EFFICIENCY MAY BE AFFECTED On certain vehicles the front brake discs may not be the required thickness for the vehicle definition. This concern may result in reduced braking efficiency.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to check and where necessary replace the front brake discs.

jeep.defect: STEERING ARMS MAY BREAK There is a possibility that due to an incorrect specification the steering arms when subjected to unusual stress such as an impact may break.
jeep.remedy: Recall affected vehicles and replace steering arms with correct specification type.

jeep.defect: BRAKES MAY FAIL Due to the possibility of a fault in the production process the flexible rubber brake hoses may not have been correctly vulcanised. As a consequence may partially or totally restrict the internal flow of the brake hydraulic fluid. Should this happen a reduction in efficiency during braking would occur.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the hoses checked to identify if they are within the affected batch. If this is the case they will be replaced with quality assured items.

jeep.defect: SUPPLEMENTARY HEATER WIRING MAY BECOME DAMAGED AND CAUSE AN ELECTRICAL SHORT-CIRCUIT On some Fiat 500L vehicles a layout non-conformity could cause abrasion of the supplementary heater (PTC) wiring. This could result in possible electric short-circuiting with the possibility of a loss of some vehicle safety. In the worst case it could cause a vehicle fire..
jeep.remedy: Apply a cut-proof sheath on the supplementary heater wiring to protect it from abrasions.

jeep.defect: FRONT WIPER MAY FAIL An internal fault with the wiper motor could cause it to stop working. In some rare cases the windscreen wipers may stop working while in operation.
jeep.remedy: Recall affected vehicles and check the manufacturing date of the wiper motor and add a supplementary earth wiring harness if necessary.

jeep.defect: BRAKES MAY FAIL Due to the possibility of a fault in the production process the flexible rubber brake hoses may not have been correctly vulcanised. As a consequence may partially or totally restrict the internal flow of the brake hydraulic fluid. Should this happen a reduction in efficiency during braking would occur.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the hoses checked to identify if they are within the affected batch. If this is the case they will be replaced with quality assured items.

jeep.defect: SIDE AIRBAG MAY NOT DEPLOY The seatbelt pre-tensioner and/or side airbag curtains may not deploy in the event of certain low speed roll over events which can lead to an increased risk of injury to vehicle occupants.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to reprogram the Occupant Restraint Control Module (ORC).

jeep.defect: LOSS OF STEERING CONTROL The steering column upper shaft fixing bolt may not have had thread locking agent applied to it during assembly. This may allow it to come loose causing a noise. In extreme cases this may result in a loss of steering control.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to check and where necessary fit a bolt affixed with pre applied locking compound.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF SERVO ASSISTANCE The steel vacuum tube that supplies vacuum to the brake booster may crack resulting in loss of servo assistance.  This will result in increased pedal power to stop the vehicle.
jeep.remedy: Recall vehicles and replace the steel vacuum tube with a flexible vacuum hose.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE FAILURE OF FRONT SPRING A specific batch of vehicles have been equipped with front suspension coil springs which may suffer from localised corrosion. This can cause breakage of the springs with an adverse effect on vehicle control.
jeep.remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original coil springs with quality assured examples.

jeep.defect: ROUTING OF BRAKE VACUUM PIPE MAY BE INCORRECT In some cases due to the non compliant routing of the brake servo vacuum supply pipe damage to the pipe may occur with the possibility that braking assistance might be reduced.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the subject pipe checked and re-routed. Should any damage be found the pipe will be replaced.

jeep.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK FROM MANIFOLD Fuel may leak as on some engines the fuel manifolds may not be to specification. If the fuel manifold leaks it is possible that a loss of power could occur and the engine cut out.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to inspect the fuel manifold and check it for conformity to specification. Where necessary replace the fuel manifold.

jeep.defect: DUE TO A NONCONFORMITY OF THE FUEL RETURN PIPE DIESEL FUEL LEAKS MAY OCCUR Due to a nonconformity of the fuel return pipe diesel fuel leaks may occur.
jeep.remedy: Check the conformity of the fuel return pipe and if necessary replace.

jeep.defect: INCORRECTLY POSITIONED FUEL PIPE Some vehicles may have been equipped with an incorrectly positioned fuel pipe.
jeep.remedy: Check fuel pipe positioning correct if necessary and fit protective sleeve.

jeep.defect: DRIVER AIRBAG MAY FAIL TO DEPLOY The driver�s airbag was manufactured with an incorrectly manufactured airbag inflator initiator that may not ignite when a deployment voltage is provided to the initiator. As a result vehicles may experience a �non-deployment� of the driver airbag during a crash event warranting an airbag deployment which could increase the risk of injury.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the driver airbag unit (initiator included) with a quality assured unit.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE DAMAGE TO BRAKE PIPES On ABS equipped Punto vehicles contact may take place between the brake compensator springs and the rear (metal) brake pipes. This could damage the pipes causing loss of brake fluid and reducing the efficiency of the service brake.
jeep.remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and secure the subject brake pipes to eliminate the possibility of any contact with the compensator springs. Any brake pipes found to be damaged will be replaced.

jeep.defect: VEHICLE MAY ROLL AWAY It has been identified that the hand brake lever may not have been manufactured to the correct specification. It could result in the vehicle rolling away.
jeep.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles and replace the hand brake assembly with a new quality controlled assembly

jeep.defect: The PBU (pressure valve) membrane in the high voltage battery pack may not be sealed due to incomplete ultrasonic welding On affected vehicles The PBU (pressure valve) membrane in the high voltage battery pack may not be sealed due to incomplete ultrasonic welding. If the battery pack is completely submerged in water (i.e. water fording) water can enter the battery pack which can cause a fire.
jeep.remedy: Check the QR code on the PBU (pressure valve) to verify the compliance of the 48V battery and replacement of the 48V battery if necessary.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF VEHICLE SAFETY FEATURES The ignition switch may unintentionally change position while driving.  This may result in a loss of engine power power steering assist power brake assist or disable the airbag function.
jeep.remedy: On affected vehicles replace the ignition switch and lock cylinder

jeep.defect: AIRBAG CIRCUIT MAY BE COMPROMISED The driver' s airbag clockspring may ingest dust. This may cause the airbag warning light to illuminate. It may also affect the air bag operation in the event of a collision.
jeep.remedy: On affected vehicles replace the air bag clock spring steering wheel back cover and steering column shrouds.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF BRAKE SERVO ASSISTANCE Vehicles may experience a vacuum leak in the EGR to Electronic Vacuum Regulator (EVM) tube. This may cause a loss of brake booster vacuum and require increased effort from the driver to operate the foot brake.
jeep.remedy: Inspect the vacuum tube from the EVM to the dash panel. Replace if damaged and re route the tube to eliminate interference with the exhaust shield.

jeep.defect: LOSS OF STEERING CONTROL The upper fork on the steering shaft fork may not have been correctly fixed/'staked' onto the shaft.  This may cause a knock from the steering and in extreme cases the fork may separate from the shaft and result in loss of steering control.
jeep.remedy: To check the shaft for the presence of the 2 'Stake' markings.

jeep.defect: BRAKING EFFICIENCY MAY BE REDUCED A connector on the brake servo pipe may fail and cause a loss of vacuum assistance necessitating the driver to include additional effort when braking.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to fit a new brake servo pipe.

jeep.defect: ANTI-ROLL BAR BUSH WEAR It has been identified that the front anti-roll bar bushes may wear after a period of time. Should this occur noise will be generated by contact between the anti-roll bar and the metal sleeve of the bush.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the front anti-roll bar replaced.

jeep.defect: INCORRECT LOAD CAPACITY LISTED FOR INTERIOR HOOKS It has been identified that the maximum load capacity for the load restraint hooks in the load compartment of the vehicle has been incorrectly written in the Owner Handbook.  The correct load capacity is 500 daN and not the 625 daN as written. If the correct load capacity of 500 daN is not adhered to then the load hooks may not retain the load due to overloading. This could result in an unsecured load with the potential for loss of control of the vehicle.
jeep.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to attach a load capacity label within the load compartment and install an additional amended page to the Owner Handbook.

jeep.defect: VEHICLE WEIGHT INFORMATION IS INCORRECT It has been identified that the vehicle manufacturer's weight label located on the driver's side B pillar contains incorrect information.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will be fitted with the correct weight label.

jeep.defect: On the affected vehicle the tightening torque applied to the steering rack during production may be insufficient. On the affected vehicle the tightening torque applied to the steering rack during production may be insufficient.
jeep.remedy: The repair is replacement of the left steering pinion tie rod retainer nut and apply the correct torque.

jeep.defect: SEAT MAY NOT PERFORM AS EXPECTED DURING A COLLISION The seat may not remain in position when subjected to greater than normal driving forces such as those involved in an impact. This may possibly cause injury to the driver/passenger seated in the right hand front seat. The right hand front seat guides may not conform to design specification and installation specifications.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and check the installation of the original seat guide. If it does not conform replace the seat cushion structure (guide).

jeep.defect: THE TRANSMISSION HARNESS MAY HAVE INSUFFICIENT CLEARANCE TO THE CATALYTIC CONVERTER Insufficient clearance between transmission harness and catalytic convertor.
jeep.remedy: Inspect the transmission wiring harness reposition harness or replace if heat damaged.

jeep.defect: FRONT BRAKE CALIPERS COULD BREAK UNDER CERTAIN OPERATING CONDITIONS. It has been identified that the front brake calipers may have been incorrectly manufactured and as such could fail under certain operating conditions.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the build codes on both front brake calipers checked. Those calipers found to be within the specified build code will be replaced.

jeep.defect: UNINTENDED AIRBAG DEPLOYMENT Following deactivation of the passenger airbag via the dashboard menu with the ignition on the passenger airbag may be reactivated following a fast cycling (less than 2 seconds) of the ignition key (on-off-on). The passenger airbag deactivation warning light would also have been switched off but the driver may not notice. In a collision and in certain conditions an unintended airbag deployment may contribute to a loss of further control or injury to driver and/or passengers.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the airbag control unit.

jeep.defect: THE START & STOP SYSTEM MAY NOT BE SET CORRECTLY AND THEREFORE MAY NOT COMPLY WITH TYPE APPROVAL REQUIREMENTS The Start & Stop system may not be set correctly and therefore may not comply with type approval requirements.
jeep.remedy: The proxi file must be updated to solve the non conformity.

jeep.defect: SHORT CIRCUIT MAY OCCUR It is possible that during the manufacturing process the coating on the Occupant Restraint Control (ORC) printed circuit may not have been applied correctly. If the coating has been applied incorrectly it can result in lead salts forming which can cause a resistive short across the ORC module printed circuit board(s). Atmospheric humidity may increase the potential for this condition to occur. Should this occur then it will cause the airbag warning lamp to illuminate and potentially disable the passive restraint system. Ultimately this can result in an inoperative passive restraint system (airbag) which could increase the risk of injury in the event of a collision.
jeep.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to replace the ORC module.

jeep.defect: POWER ASSISTANCE TO STEERING MAY BE LOST The wiring for the power steering electric pump may interfere with the edge of the left front wheel arch. This may cause damage to the wiring and a loss of power steering assistance.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected so the wiring can be placed in a protective pipe. The wiring and pipe will then be secured in the correct position.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE INTERFERENCE BETWEEN FUEL SUPPLY AND RETURN LINES Possible interference between the fuel supply and return lines.
jeep.remedy: Reposition the pipes to avoid interference.

jeep.defect: UNDERBONNET FIRE CONCERN Debris may accumulate on the exhaust manifold.  This could lead to an under bonnet fire.
jeep.remedy: Install an intake/exhaust manifold debris shield.

jeep.defect: FUEL LEAKAGE MAY OCCUR FROM THE FUEL TANK Due to a non-conformity in production fuel leakage may occur from the fuel tank
jeep.remedy: Replace the fuel tank

jeep.defect: INADVERTENT DEPLOYMENT OF A FRONT AIRBAG The Occupant Restraint Control (ORC) module may allow a front airbag and/or seatbelt pretensioner to inadvertently deploy.
jeep.remedy: On affected vehicles replace the ORC Module. Due to issues with parts supply the recall of  WG/WJ models is suspended however KJ models remain unaffected.

jeep.defect: POTENTIAL FIRE The fuel return pipe connector at the injectors may overtime wear and leak. The leaking fuel is a fire risk and also could be hazardous to other road users.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the fuel return pipe.

jeep.defect: SECURITY OF SEAT BELT A number of the subject vehicles have been fitted with seat belts manufactured by TRW the attachment systems of which may not remain secure in an accident situation.
jeep.remedy: Recall the affected vehicles check the date of production on the seat belt buckles and replace those within the critical batch.

jeep.defect: POTENTIAL MOVEMENT OF THE BATTERY Potential movement of the battery and consequent breakage of the battery wires.
jeep.remedy: A battery spacer must be fitted

jeep.defect: FIRE MAY OCCUR Water intrusion into the power liftgate module electrical connectors can lead to corrosion and higher resistance. This condition can cause the module to become inoperative and/or cause a fire.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected. The vehicles will be inspected for evidence of water intrusion and electrical connector corrosion. The vehicle will be repaired to eliminate the possibility of further water intrusion. On vehicles found with corrosion in the power liftgate module electrical connectors the module and electrical connectors will be replaced. All the vehicles will receive a power liftgate module water shield.

jeep.defect: HANDBRAKE CONCERN The handbrake cable may have been incorrectly fitted and could become disconnected from the rear brake mechanism.  This would result in the handbrake becoming ineffective.
jeep.remedy: Check that the handbrake cable is correctly connected to the rear brake mechanism and fit a new cable where it is not.

jeep.defect: ACCELERATOR MAY STICK It has been identified that the possibility exists that the accelerator pedal's rotation pin may not have been inserted correctly. In this condition the accelerator pedal might stick.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the accelerator pedal checked for the presence of the pin. Should the pin be found to be missing the accelerator pedal will be changed.

jeep.defect: ELECTRONIC BRAKE CONTROL MODULE MAY ALLOW A MOMENTARY DELAY IN BRAKE APPLICATION. It has been established that the software programmed into the electronic brake control module (EBC) may permit a momentary delay in brake application when coasting uphill during certain conditions.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the EBC reprogrammed.

jeep.defect: ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS MAY BE DEACTIVATED In some circumstances the driver and passenger may experience consequent switching off of the instrument panel light and possible deactivation of other electronic systems such as the ABS and airbags. The concern is caused by loose connections at the ignition switch contact holder block.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the ignition switch contact holder block.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF BRAKE SERVO ASSISTANCE After extended high speed running brake servo assistance may be lost due to petrol contamination of the servo diaphragm.
jeep.remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the servo brake vacuum pipe and checking of the brake servo efficiency.

jeep.defect: SEAT MAY NOT PERFORM CORRECTLY IN A COLLISION Front and/or rear seats may have been fitted with incorrectly tightened fasteners. This may increase risk of injury to occupants during a collision.
jeep.remedy: Replace affected seat assemblies.

jeep.defect: ELECTRONIC BRAKE CONTROL MODULE MAY ALLOW A MOMENTARY DELAY IN BRAKE APPLICATION. It has been established that the software programmed into the electronic brake control module (EBC) may permit a momentary delay in brake application when coasting uphill during certain conditions.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the EBC reprogrammed.

jeep.defect: BRAKES MAY FAIL Front inner fender liners may detach or sag allowing fender liner to contact brake pipes.  Continuous fender liner contact with the brake pipes could result in a hydraulic leak and reduce brake performance.  This loss in brake performance could cause a crash without warning.
jeep.remedy: Modify and refit fender liners securing clips.  If required renew brake pipes.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF BRAKE SERVO ASSISTANCE Vehicles may experience a loss of power assistance to the brakes due to a collapsed brake booster vacuum hose. This will result in increased effort being required from the driver to apply the foot brake.
jeep.remedy: Inspect the brake booster vacuum hose. If damaged the hose will be replaced. In either case the hose will be re routed to eliminate interference with the coolant recovery pipe.

jeep.defect: FRONT SEATBELTS MAY NOT FUNCTION AS INTENDED It has been identified that the front seatbelt anchorage links may not have been manufactured to the correct specification. If the link is subjected to an abnormal force then it may not perform as required.
jeep.remedy: Recall all the affected vehicles to check the link and if required replace it.

jeep.defect: SUSPENSION COIL SPRING MAY BREAK Under environmental conditions that require intensive use of salt on the roads corrosive deposits accumulate inside the noise-insulating protective sheath located on the front suspension springs creating areas of corrosion which may lead to the spring breaking after a period of time.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the front coil springs with those of a new type.

jeep.defect: REAR LOWER CONTROL ARM MAY EXPERIENCE EXCESSIVE CORROSION The rear lower control arms may experience excessive corrosion eventually resulting in a fracture A fractured rear control arm could cause reduced vehicle control and can cause a vehicle crash without prior warning
jeep.remedy: Replace both rear lower control arms

jeep.defect: The Hydraulic Control Unit (HCU/ABS) Anti-lock Brake System module may have been built with a Hydraulic Control Unit (HCU/ABS) Anti-lock Brake System module that falsely reads pressure in the primary circuit. The Hydraulic Control Unit (HCU/ABS) Anti-lock Brake System module may have been built with a Hydraulic Control Unit (HCU/ABS) Anti-lock Brake System module that falsely reads pressure in the primary circuit.
jeep.remedy: The repair is the installation of new software to the HCU/ABS module.

jeep.defect: ACCELERATOR PEDAL CONCERN The accelerator pedal may foul on its travel limiting stop and prevent the engine from decellerating when the pedal is released.
jeep.remedy: Fit a modified pedal travel limiting stop.

jeep.defect: VEHICLE SHORT  CAUSING CAN-C BUS TO STOP COMMUNICATING A short in the vehicle causing the CAN-C bus to stop communicating while the cruise control is active and the vehicle speed is below the set speed such that the cruise control system is requesting positive torque at the exact moment of the short it is possible for a positive torque request to be locked on the PCM.   This may result in either the vehicle maintaining its current speed or possibly accelerating.
jeep.remedy: Inspect the software level of the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) and if necessary reprogram the PCM

jeep.defect: THE ENGINE MAY LOSE ITS ABILITY TO SYNCHRONIZE INJECTOR PULSES AND CAMSHAFT TIMING The engine may lose its ability to synchronize injector pulses and camshaft timing.
jeep.remedy: Reprogram the Powertrain Control Module to maintain engine operation if the signal material is lost.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE DAMAGE TO BRAKE PIPES On ABS equipped Punto vehicles contact may take place between the brake compensator springs and the rear (metal) brake pipes. This could damage the pipes causing loss of brake fluid and reducing the efficiency of the service brake.
jeep.remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and secure the subject brake pipes to eliminate the possibility of any contact with the compensator springs. Any brake pipes found to be damaged will be replaced.

jeep.defect: WATER INGRESS INTO THE AIRBAG ECU Water ingress into the airbag control unit (ECU) could result in illumination of the warning light and in the worst case unintentional deployment of the airbag.
jeep.remedy: Seal the airbag ECU compartment

jeep.defect: VEHICLE MAY ROLL AWAY The automatic transmission may shift into or through neutral unintentionally when parked which in some circumstances could allow the vehicle to move/runaway.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to attach a software update to remove possibility of inadvertent shifting.

jeep.defect: STEERING SWIVEL  JOINT MAY FAIL RESULTING IN LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL The possibility exists that the swivel joint stem of the front suspension vertical links maybe of an incorrect size. This can lead to the generation of noise whilst driving and the possibility of suspension disconnection following a violent impact to the front axle and subsequent loss of vehicle control.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the swivel joint stems checked for the presence of play and will be replaced if any is found.

jeep.defect: VEHICLES MAY HAVE BEEN FITTED WITH THE FRONT CROSSMEMBER INCORRECTLY TIGHTENED Vehicles may have been fitted with the front crossmember incorrectly tightened.
jeep.remedy: Check and tighten the bolts on the front crossmember to the prescribed torque. Replacement of the steering rack if necessary.

jeep.defect: FRONT WINDSCREEN WIPERS MAY BECOME INOPERATIVE It has been identified that the possibility exists that water may ingress into the front windscreen wiper motor. Should this occur the wipers may become inoperative. In conditions of poor visibility this may result in impaired driver visibility.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the front windscreen wiper motor fitted with a protective cover.

jeep.defect: EGR PIPE COULD FRACTURE DUE TO A POTENTIAL NON-CONFORMITY The EGR pipe could fracture due to a potential non-conformity the fractured pipe may damage the alternator resulting in a loss of battery voltage and potentially a loss of engine power.
jeep.remedy: The pipe must be checked and if incorrect replaced with a new  part.

jeep.defect: FRONT BRAKE CALIPERS COULD BREAK UNDER CERTAIN OPERATING CONDITIONS. It has been identified that the front brake calipers may have been incorrectly manufactured and as such could fail under certain operating conditions.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the build codes on both front brake calipers checked. Those calipers found to be within the specified build code will be replaced.

jeep.defect: INEFFECTIVE/INCORRECT TIGHTENING OF A LOCK NUT ON THE STEERING GEAR ROD Vehicles may have been produced with ineffective/incorrect tightening of a lock nut on the steering gear rod.
jeep.remedy: Check for the correct tightening of the lock nut and check/adjust wheel alignment if tightening was required.

jeep.defect: FRONT SEAT SHOULDER BELTS ADJUSTABLE ANCHORS MAY HAVE INADEQUATE STRENGTH The front shoulder belt adjustable anchors on affected vehicles may have been improperly manufactured and could have inadequate strength. An anchor with inadequate strength may allow the front shoulder belt to separate from the anchor under certain accident conditions.
jeep.remedy: To correct this condition both front shoulder belt adjustable anchors must be replaced.

jeep.defect: LOSS OF BRAKING EFFICIENCY A defective retaining clip may allow the throttle cable to chafe against certain rigid brake pipes. This could damage the pipes and result in a reduction in braking efficiency.
jeep.remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the subject retaining clip replaced with a modified version.

jeep.defect: VEHICLES MAY HAVE BEEN FITTED WITH A FAULTY LEFT OR RIGHT SIDE HALF-SHAFT A number of vehicles may have been fitted with a faulty left or right side half-shaft (drive shaft).
jeep.remedy: The half-shaft identified as faulty according to traceability data must be replaced

jeep.defect: INSTRUMENT CLUSTER MAY DISPLAY INCORRECT INFORMATION Due to a nonconformity in the production process the instrument cluster may stick and display incorrect speed information.
jeep.remedy: On affected vehicles replace the instrument cluster.

jeep.defect: WATER INGRESS TO ABS CONTROL UNIT Water may enter the ABS (antilock brake) control unit through a harness connector. This will cause the ABS control unit to malfunction and the fault warning lamp to illuminate.
jeep.remedy: Fit a new ABS wiring harness which has watertight connectors.

jeep.defect: THE BRAKE LINE RETAINING CLIP MAY NOT BE FIXED CORRECTLY TO THE TUCKER ON THE DASHBOARD The brake line (pipe) may not be fixed correctly
jeep.remedy: Check the clip is fixed correctly and replace damaged brake pipes

jeep.defect: HEADLIGHT DIRECTIONAL CONTROL MAY FAIL The Body Control Module (BCM) may have incorrect headlamp levelling parameters. This can result in headlamp levelling switch operation being the opposite of the headlamp directional movement desired. This could cause a crash without warning.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and the headlamp levelling parameters will be reprogrammed within the BCM.

jeep.defect: STEERING ARMS MAY BREAK There is a possibility that due to an incorrect specification the steering arms when subjected to unusual stress such as an impact may break.
jeep.remedy: Recall affected vehicles and replace steering arms with correct specification type.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE SEPARATION OF FRONT SUSPENSION BALL JOINT Water may enter the front suspension ball joints this can cause the ball joint to corrode and separate.
jeep.remedy: Replace any corroded ball joints and fit dirt/water shields to all vehicles.

jeep.defect: DOOR LOCKS MAY MALFUNCTION AND ALLOW DOORS TO OPEN UNINTENTIONALLY On a number of Fiat Fullback vehicles in some weather conditions (high temperatures) the mechanism inside the door lock may not function as intended. This can allow the door(s) to open unintentionally.
jeep.remedy: The door locks must be replaced with compliant components.

jeep.defect: REAR SUSPENSION MAY FAIL During the assembly of the vehicle it is possible the right hand rear suspension coil spring was damaged. Over time any damage could lead to the failure of the coil spring.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to inspect and where necessary replace the coil spring.

jeep.defect: FRONT SEAT HEATING ELEMENTS MAY OVERHEAT It has been identified that the front seat heating elements may overheat. This in extreme circumstances may result in an interior fire.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have both front seat heating elements replaced.

jeep.defect: BRAKE BOOSTER WATER SHIELD MAY BE INCORRECTLY INSTALLED There is a risk that the brake booster water shield may be incorrectly installed. This may result in  limited braking ability due to water ingress into the brake booster.
jeep.remedy: On affected vehicles the brake booster water shield must be inspected for proper installation. If the brake booster water shield is found to be missing or incorrectly installed the brake booster must also be vacuum tested. Brake boosters that do not pass the vacuum test must be replaced. At the conclusion of this the brake booster must be equipped with a properly installed shield to protect the brake booster crimp joints from water exposure.

jeep.defect: ENGINE MAY CUT OUT AND OR FAIL TO RESTART It has been identified that the wireless control module may fail with the result that the engine may fail to start or cut out.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the wireless control module replaced.

jeep.defect: FRONT HUB SECURITY Front hub nut security pin may have been incorrectly fitted.
jeep.remedy: Recall affected vehicles check for correct fitment of pin and replace if necessary

jeep.defect: UNINTENDED AIRBAG DEPLOYMENT Following deactivation of the passenger airbag via the dashboard menu with the ignition on the passenger airbag may be reactivated following a fast cycling (less than 2 seconds) of the ignition key (on-off-on). The passenger airbag deactivation warning light would also have been switched off but the driver may not notice. In a collision and in certain conditions an unintended airbag deployment may contribute to a loss of further control or injury to driver and/or passengers.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the airbag control unit.

jeep.defect: SIDE AIRBAG MAY NOT DEPLOY The side air bags may not deploy in a side impact as designed.
jeep.remedy: Recall affected vehicles and replace air bag.

jeep.defect: INTERIOR FAN WIRING MAY CHAFE ON DASHBOARD SUPPORT The interior fan wiring may chafe on a dashboard support.  This could result in a short circuit and a fire in the fan unit.
jeep.remedy: Fit additional insulation and protection to the fan electrical  wiring.

jeep.defect: POSSIBILITY THAT THE ACCELERATOR PEDAL COULD FOUL ON THE FLOOR Possibility that the accelerator may foul on the floor mounted pedal stop
jeep.remedy: Recall likely to be affected vehicles and fit a modified throttle pedal stop.

jeep.defect: ENGINE MAY CUT OUT The engine may cut out because the pipe connecting the tanks has been incorrectly manufactured which can stop the fuel transfer from the secondary tank to the primary tank. The fuel gauge will read that there is fuel in the tank when this occurs.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to replace the fuel transfer pipe.

jeep.defect: FIRE MAY OCCUR The layout of the ABS wiring maybe incorrect in the area of the battery holding unit.  The wiring may on some vehicles maybe trapped and pinched exposing wiring in some area.  this may cause damage and in extreme cases a potential risk of fire.
jeep.remedy: Repair to inspect and repair the wiring using industry accepted soldered connectors

jeep.defect: DAYTIME RUNNING LAMP FUNCTIONS INCORRECTLY WHEN INDICATOR IS ACTIVATED. It is possible that the Daytime Running Lamps (DRL) do not function correctly when the turn signal indicator is actuated.  The opposite DRL (rather than adjacent) may turn off when the turn signal is activated.  This could result in confusion for other road users.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to check the function of the lights and where necessary modify the wiring.

jeep.defect: POSSIBIITY OF FIRE IN THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT A fire might occur in the engine compartment as a result of the waste gate excess pressure pipe being incorrectly routed.
jeep.remedy: Recall the vehicle that are likely to be affected to ensure the waste gate pipe is correctly routed and fixed in the appropriate clips.

jeep.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF STEERING Excess play between steering rack and pinion leading to noise and possible loss of steering when parking.
jeep.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the steering pinion bearing preload adjusted or the steering rack assembly will be replaced as necessary

jinan.defect: FRONT BRAKE DISC MOUNTING BOLTS MAY NOT BE FULLY SECURE The front brake disc mounting bolts may not have been fully tightened at the factory. Additionally the rear wheel spokes may not have been fully tightened.
jinan.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to check the torque of the front brake disc mounting bolts and then to replace the bolts with thread locked bolts and torquing to specification. Check the tension of the rear wheel spokes and where necessary tighten the rear wheel spokes.

john.defect: STEERING MAY FAIL The steering shaft has the potential to separate from the steering rack assembly. If this occurs it may result in a loss of vehicle steering control.
john.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and ensure the locating plate is fitted correctly. An additional plate will be fitted to ensure the locating plate cannot come out of its fixing.

john.defect: STEERING MAY FAIL The steering shaft has the potential to separate from the steering rack assembly. If this occurs it may result in a loss of vehicle steering control.
john.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and ensure the locating plate is fitted correctly. An additional plate will be fitted to ensure the locating plate cannot come out of its fixing.

john.defect: STEERING MAY FAIL The steering shaft has the potential to separate from the steering rack assembly. If this occurs it may result in a loss of vehicle steering control.
john.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and ensure the locating plate is fitted correctly. An additional plate will be fitted to ensure the locating plate cannot come out of its fixing.

john.defect: STEERING MAY FAIL The steering shaft has the potential to separate from the steering rack assembly. If this occurs it may result in a loss of vehicle steering control.
john.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and ensure the locating plate is fitted correctly. An additional plate will be fitted to ensure the locating plate cannot come out of its fixing.

john.defect: POSSIBLE EXCESSIVE BRAKE PEDAL TRAVEL Possible excessive brake pedal travel.
john.remedy: Addition of check valve to prevent leak down of fluid

johnston.defect: FIT MISSING SEAT BELTS Due to changes in UK legislation vehicles manufactured between October 2001 and December 2004 are required to be fitted with driver and passenger seat belts.
johnston.remedy: Recalled vehicles will be fitted with the requisite number of seat belts.

johnston.defect: HOPPER MAY DETACH WHEN BEING TIPPED It has been identified that the area of the sweeper hopper immediately in front or behind of the tipping brackets can crack/fracture. In extreme cases this could result in the hopper detaching when or whilst being tipped.
johnston.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to be inspected and for the fitment of a reaction beam.

johnston.defect: HOPPER MAY DETACH WHEN BEING TIPPED It has been identified that the area of the sweeper hopper immediately in front or behind of the tipping brackets can crack/fracture. In extreme cases this could result in the hopper detaching when or whilst being tipped.
johnston.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to be inspected and for the fitment of a reaction beam.

johnston.defect: STEERING COLUMN MAY FAIL There is a possibility of the steering column failing. The recall includes the vehicles that have had the steering column replaced under a previous recall notice.
johnston.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the steering column with one that has been tested and certified.

jonckheere.defect: EMERGENCY DOOR MAY JAM WHEN OPENED The emergency exit door does not fit flush into it's aperture at the top edge. This can cause the door to jam in the frame when being opened.
jonckheere.remedy: Fit a dovetail guide plate at the top of the door frame.

juratek.defect: BRAKES MAY FAIL The affected brake discs have been incorrectly machined in that the corner undercut has been over machined to a depth of 9mm reducing the wall thickness. Braking surfaces can separate from the mounting with a consequent loss of braking.
juratek.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the brake discs.

kassbohrer.defect: CRACKING OF FRONT AXLE HUBS Isolated instances of cracking of the front hubs have been recorded on high mileage vehicles.
kassbohrer.remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the subject hubs with modified versions.

kato.defect: WHEEL MAY DETACH There is a possibility that the front and or rear wheel hubs may crack which in the worst case could lead to wheel loss.
kato.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to inspect and dependant on type change the wheel hubs.

kato.defect: CLUTCH MAY FAIL There is a possibility that the clutch housing may crack which could in the worst case lead to the gearbox falling out of the chassis.
kato.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to change the clutch housing to a cast type. If cracked housing are found it may also be necessary to also fit a new flywheel housing.

kawasaki.defect: Motor drive battery packs inspection – Recall On affected motorcycles there is a risk the terminals of the motor drive battery packs may become dislodged during plugging or unplugging of the battery packs due to a manufacturing error.
kawasaki.remedy: Inspect and replace battery packs if necessary.

kawasaki.defect: Motor drive battery packs inspection – Recall On affected motorcycles there is a risk the terminals of the motor drive battery packs may become dislodged during plugging or unplugging of the battery packs due to a manufacturing error.
kawasaki.remedy: Inspect and replace battery packs if necessary.

kawasaki.defect: LOWER COWLING MAY IMPEDE BRAKING The foot may be impeded when operating the rear brake operating lever effectively by the top edge of the lower cowling. This could cause longer than expected stopping distances.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the right hand foot guard and lower cowling bracket.

kawasaki.defect: OIL MAY LEAK Oil may leak from the rear shock absorber which may get on the rear tyre and cause a lack of adhesion tyre to road.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to fit a new shock absorber.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL The engine ECU may have the incorrect settings installed which could cause the engine to stall and cause the rider to loose control of the machine.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall all affected machines and change the engine ECU.

kawasaki.defect: REAR BRAKE HOSE AND/OR REAR WHEEL ROTATION SENSOR LEAD MAY TOUCH REAR TYRE DUE TO INCORRECT ROUTING Due to incorrect routing the rear brake hose and / or the rear wheel rotation sensor lead may touch the rear tyre.
kawasaki.remedy: Inspect and re-route the hose and lead as needed replace the rear brake hose and / or sensor lead if they are damaged.

kawasaki.defect: FRONT SUSPENSION MAY COLLAPSE AND LOSS OF STEERING CONTROL There is a possibility that the front lower suspension swivel joints may fracture. If this occurs steering control will be lost.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace both of the front lower suspension swivel joints.

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF TYRE PRESSURE FROM FRONT AND REAR TYRES The tyre valve nut on the front and rear wheels can crack from a combination of stress and corrosion. Because the affected units are fitted tubeless tyres cracking of the nut can lead to a reduction of tyre pressure. This could adversely affect the handling and performance of the vehicle and may create a risk of an accident possibly resulting in personal injury.
kawasaki.remedy: Fit replacement tyre valve nuts of increased size and improved material. Replace washer beneath the valve nut with one of improved material.

kawasaki.defect: FOOT REST MAY DETACH The circlips securing the passenger footrest pivot may be brittle due to a manufacturing error.  This can cause the circlip to fail allowing the pivot pins to come out of position and the footrest to come off while riding creating the potential for an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Replacement of circlips on both passenger footrests.

kawasaki.defect: OIL MAY LEAK On eligible units of Ninja ZX-10R and Ninja ZX-10R ABS models some engine crankcases may have a casting flaw which allows engine oil to leak at the starter motor mounting area and collect on the crankcase surface. Continued use in this condition can allow oil to get onto the rear tyre
kawasaki.remedy: The repair consists of adding a special sealing compound to the affected area to avoid any possibility of oil leakage.

kawasaki.defect: 1) FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN 2) STOWAGE OF TOOLS IN COMPARTMENT (ZX600-F1 MODEL ONLY) 1) As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. 2) Items or tools placed in the document/tool kit compartment may fall from the compartment into the drive chain area. (ZX600 - F1 model only).
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and:- A) Replace the drive chain with a quality assured version. B) Replace the tool bag and mounting strap with modified versions and fit an additional cover (ZX600-F1 model only).

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBILITY OF AN OIL LEAK. During cold starts the oil pressure relief valve may not respond quickly enough thus allowing excess pressure to build up causing the bottom of the oil filter to deform. This can cause oil to leak from the filter with the potential of a slip type accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall likely to be affected machines and fit a replacement oil filter.

kawasaki.defect: REAR BRAKE MAY FAIL On eligible units of 1400 GTR and 1400GTR ABS models small stones or other road debris can become trapped between the rear brake pedal and guard and prevent the pedal from fully releasing. This can cause over heating potentially leading to rear brake damage and lock up or failure of the rear brake. On 14  GTR ABS models with K-ACT the front brake may also be affected because it is linked with rear brake operation.
kawasaki.remedy: The repair consists of replacing the rear master cylinder rod end and removing the guard.

kawasaki.defect: THE FRONT BRAKE HOSE COULD BECOME WEDGED BETWEEN THE FRONT FORK AND THE FENDER There is a possibility that the front brake hose could become wedged between the front fork and the fender. The brake hose may suffer abrasion damage.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall affected machines check brake hose replace if necessary and fit brake hose clamp

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBILITY OF AN OIL LEAK. During cold starts the oil pressure relief valve may not respond quickly enough thus allowing excess pressure to build up causing the bottom of the oil filter to deform. This can cause oil to leak from the filter with the potential of a slip type accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall likely to be affected machines and fit a replacement oil filter.

kawasaki.defect: RISK OF FIRE It has been identified that on subject machines the fuel hose may not have been properly connected to the fuel injector delivery pipe creating the possibility of a fuel leak resulting in the risk of fire or an explosion.
kawasaki.remedy: Recalled machines will be inspected to ensure that the fuel hose has been properly secured to the fuel rail. The fuel hose will be replaced if the clip is damaged and will not lock correctly.

kawasaki.defect: 1) FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN 2) STOWAGE OF TOOLS IN COMPARTMENT (ZX600-F1 MODEL ONLY) 1) As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. 2) Items or tools placed in the document/tool kit compartment may fall from the compartment into the drive chain area. (ZX600 - F1 model only).
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and:- A) Replace the drive chain with a quality assured version. B) Replace the tool bag and mounting strap with modified versions and fit an additional cover (ZX600-F1 model only).

kawasaki.defect: THE WIRING HARNESS FOR THE HORN MAY NOT BE DURABLE ENOUGH The wiring harness for the horn may not be durable enough.�
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the horn and bracket on all units and to modify the wiring harness.

kawasaki.defect: ABS MAY NOT FUNCTION CORRECTLY The ABS system may not function correctly causing longer stopping distances than expected and also the fault may not illuminate the ABS warning lamp. This is due to a none conformance on production with the ABS unit.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and replace the ABS unit.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY CUT OUT The operation of the vehicle down sensor under certain conditions may be affected by vibration through it's mounting and cause the engine to cut out.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the mounting of the down sensor.

kawasaki.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK The fuel tank may be deformed by the influence of varying temperature conditions fuel used and material thickness. Such deformation could cause a leak at the fuel tap mounting area leading to a potential fire risk.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the fuel tank and fuel tap O ring

kawasaki.defect: THE AMOUNT OF GREASE APPLIED TO THE NEEDLE BEARINGS IN THE REAR HUB HOUSING MAY BE INSUFFICIENT The amount of grease applied to the needle-bearings in the rear hub housing may be insufficient.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the rear hub housing needle bearing on all eligible units.

kawasaki.defect: POSSBILE FAILURE OF SUSPENSION/STEERING It has been established that a significant impact to either front wheel whilst the steering is on full lock can result in deformation of the steering ball joint mounting hole within the steering knuckle. Over time the ball joint can become loose in the knuckle and cause the mounting hole to wear. Continued use of the vehicle in this condition may eventually lead to separation of the ball joint resulting in suspension/steering failure and the potential for an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: It is the intention to recall all likely to be affected machines and change the subject steering components. However before this is done Kawasaki will inform owners of the need to check the suspension and steering before riding the machine and comprehensive instructions on how to do this are to be issued. It should be noted that if any free play is found within the steering knuckle the machine should not be ridden until such time as the re-work is carried out.

kawasaki.defect: The plunger in the camshaft-chain tensioner can lock up during usage due to deterioration of internal parts The plunger in the camshaft-chain tensioner can lock up during usage due to deterioration of internal parts.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the camshaft chain tensioner with a revised part.

kawasaki.defect: THE ELECTRONIC CONTROL UNIT DOESN'T CONTROL THE SUDDEN INCREASE IN ENGINE RPM The electronic control unit (ECU) doesn�t control the sudden increase in engine rpm if the transmission gear is not properly engaged
kawasaki.remedy: Reprogramme the ECU on all eligible units to control the sudden rpm surge.

kawasaki.defect: REAR BRAKE LIGHT MAY FAIL Vibrations can cause the tail / brake light bulb socket to displace and come away from the lamp assembly.
kawasaki.remedy: On affected machines replace the light socket with a quality assured unit.

kawasaki.defect: FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. This campaign includes some machines already actioned under recall RM95/2 which may have been fitted with incorrect chains at that time.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and replace the drive chain with a quality assured version.

kawasaki.defect: CARBURETTOR FLOAT MAY STICK CAUSING A FUEL LEAK On affected machines carburettor float may stick causing a fuel leak.
kawasaki.remedy: Inspect and if necessary modify the carburettor.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL The engine may stall due to premature wear of a bearing in the fuel pump. Prior to failure an abnormal noise will occur and continued use of the machine in this condition could lead to decreased engine power and eventual failure of the bearing.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the fuel pump with a new one.

kawasaki.defect: FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. This campaign includes some machines already actioned under recall RM95/2 which may have been fitted with incorrect chains at that time.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and replace the drive chain with a quality assured version.

kawasaki.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK FROM FUEL TAP WHEN OPERATED On affected machines fuel may leak from the fuel tap when it is operated.
kawasaki.remedy: Installation of a new fuel tap.

kawasaki.defect: REAR BRAKE HOSE AND/OR REAR WHEEL ROTATION SENSOR LEAD MAY TOUCH REAR TYRE DUE TO INCORRECT ROUTING Due to incorrect routing the rear brake hose and / or the rear wheel rotation sensor lead may touch the rear tyre.
kawasaki.remedy: Inspect and re-route the hose and lead as needed replace the rear brake hose and / or sensor lead if they are damaged.

kawasaki.defect: TRANSMISSION MAY FAIL The strength of some gears in the transmission may not be sufficient and could break if they receive excessive impact force during shifting. Drive could be lost and In the worst case the transmission may lock.
kawasaki.remedy: On affected machines replace the 2nd 3rd and 4th output gears and the 2nd input gear

kawasaki.defect: TYRE MAY DEFLATE During the manufacturing process the inner tubes may be pinched and in the worst case holed. This could cause tyre deflation and creates an increased risk the rider could lose control of the machine.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to check and where necessary replace the inner tubes.

kawasaki.defect: FUEL HOSE MAY LEAK The protective sleeve on the fuel hose from the fuel filter to the throttle assembly may not prevent damage to the hose by rubbing against the fuel pump plate. A fuel leak might occur with a risk of fire.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall affected motorcycles to replace the fuel hose with a modified type.

kawasaki.defect: FRONT WHEEL MAY CONTAIN CASTING FLAWS. There is a possibility that the front wheel could contain casting flaws which could potentially lead to failure.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall affected machines and replace front wheel.

kawasaki.defect: CARBURETTOR DIAPHRAGM FAILURE COULD RESULT IN FUEL LEAK Carburettor accelerator pump diaphragm may break resulting in a fuel leak and possible risk of fire.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the accelerator pump diaphragm.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY FAIL The main wiring harness can can rub against the rear of the motorcycle frame this can cause the engine to stop running and leave the rider in a vunerable situation.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall vehicles to inspect and re-route harness if harness damaged this will be repaired or replaced.

kawasaki.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK It is possible that the fuel pump bracket may have been installed incorrectly. This can cause the fuel hose to chaff on the air box resulting in damage to the hose and a possible fuel leak.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall all the affected vehicles for inspection and if required the repositioning of the bracket plus the replacement of the fuel hose.

kawasaki.defect: THE FACTORY ECU PROGRAMMING MAY CAUSE THE ENGINE TO AFTER FIRE WHEN KAWASAKI QUICK SHIFTER IS USED UNDER HEAVY ENGINE LOAD The factory Electronic Control Unit programming may cause the engine to after fire when Kawasaki Quick Shifter is used under heavy engine load.
kawasaki.remedy: Reprogram the ECU. Replace the reed valves in the air suction valve assemblies on used motorcycles and if necessary replace any parts that have been heat damaged as a result of after-fire occurring.

kawasaki.defect: REAR SHOCK ABSORBER MAY FAIL CAUSING LOSS OF CONTROL OF THE MACHINE The rear suspension unit has a possible assembly defect in that the piston-shaft nut has in some cases not been correctly tightened. If a defective suspension unit is fitted there could be an oil leak or a loss of damping control which can adversely affect the handling of the machine.
kawasaki.remedy: The owner is given a web-address to follow and access the necessary information to acertain if the shock absorber is definately affected and what to do if it is in the affected range. If your shock absorber is affected by the recall please contact the �hlins distributor in your country for an appointment to have your shock absorber corrected.

kawasaki.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK FROM FUEL TAP WHEN OPERATED On affected machines fuel may leak from the fuel tap when it is operated.
kawasaki.remedy: Installation of a new fuel tap.

kawasaki.defect: 1) FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN 2) STOWAGE OF TOOLS IN COMPARTMENT (ZX600-F1 MODEL ONLY) 1) As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. 2) Items or tools placed in the document/tool kit compartment may fall from the compartment into the drive chain area. (ZX600 - F1 model only).
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and:- A) Replace the drive chain with a quality assured version. B) Replace the tool bag and mounting strap with modified versions and fit an additional cover (ZX600-F1 model only).

kawasaki.defect: THE OIL PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE MAY FAIL The oil pressure relief valve may fail resulting in low oil pressure.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the oil pressure relief valve.

kawasaki.defect: REAR CARRIER MAY BECOME DETATCHED In certain circumstances it is possible that the genuine accessory luggage carrier could break. In the worst case the carrier and luggage could become detached from the motorcycle creating the potential for an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the luggage rack with one that has been newly designed and reinforced.

kawasaki.defect: THE WIRING HARNESS FOR THE HORN MAY NOT BE DURABLE ENOUGH The wiring harness for the horn may not be durable enough.�
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the horn and bracket on all units and to modify the wiring harness.

kawasaki.defect: SEPARATION OF THE FRAME CROSS PIPE. It is possible that the engine mounting adjustment collars have been over tightened during production. In the affected machines in certain circumstances it is possible for the frame lower cross pipe to crack and if left unattended the cross pipe could separate resulting in the potential for an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to check the torque of the engine mounting collars and where necessary retorque them. If the mountings have been over tightened the engine mounting frame will have to be removed for inspection and replaced where necessary.

kawasaki.defect: THE EXHAUST PIPE MIGHT BE INCORRECTLY SECURED The exhaust pipe might be incorrectly secured.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the exhaust collars and gaskets and tighten the nuts with a new sequence and a higher torque.

kawasaki.defect: OIL PASSAGE HOLES IN THE OIL FILTER HOUSING MAY BE INCORRECTLY MACHINED There is a possibility that the oil passage holes in the oil filter housing have not been correctly machined.
kawasaki.remedy: If the oil passage holes have not been correctly machined the engine assembly will be replaced.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL The insulation on the ignition switch harness may rub on the underside of the fuel tank. This can lead to an electrical short which may cause the engine to stall and increase the risk of injury to the rider pillion and other road users.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and inspect the ignition wiring located under the fuel tank. Where necessary the ignition switch (wiring attached) will be replaced. A wiring protection kit will be installed on all machines.

kawasaki.defect: MACHINE MAY STALL It is possible that an internal fault in the engine Electronic Control Unit (ECU) may cause the engine to stall. This can lead to a loss of control of the machine.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall all affected machines and replace the engine ECU with a reprogrammed unit.

kawasaki.defect: THE AMOUNT OF GREASE APPLIED TO THE NEEDLE BEARINGS IN THE REAR HUB HOUSING MAY BE INSUFFICIENT The amount of grease applied to the needle-bearings in the rear hub housing may be insufficient.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the rear hub housing needle bearing on all eligible units.

kawasaki.defect: FOOT REST MAY DETACH The circlips securing the passenger footrest pivot may be brittle due to a manufacturing error.  This can cause the circlip to fail allowing the pivot pins to come out of position and the footrest to come off while riding creating the potential for an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Replacement of circlips on both passenger footrests.

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF TYRE PRESSURE FROM FRONT AND REAR TYRES The tyre valve nut on the front and rear wheels can crack from a combination of stress and corrosion. Because the affected units are fitted tubeless tyres cracking of the nut can lead to a reduction of tyre pressure. This could adversely affect the handling and performance of the vehicle and may create a risk of an accident possibly resulting in personal injury.
kawasaki.remedy: Fit replacement tyre valve nuts of increased size and improved material. Replace washer beneath the valve nut with one of improved material.

kawasaki.defect: Improper programming of transmission shift control system On affected machines there is a risk that the motorcycle may shift to neutral when the rider attempts to shift from 1st to 2nd gear due to improper programming of the shift control system.
kawasaki.remedy: Update the shift control system with modified software.

kawasaki.defect: Improper programming of transmission shift control system On affected machines there is a risk that the motorcycle may shift to neutral when the rider attempts to shift from 1st to 2nd gear due to improper programming of the shift control system.
kawasaki.remedy: Update the shift control system with modified software.

kawasaki.defect: Re – tightening of the crankcase fastening bolts On affected motorcycles the crankcase fastening bolts may have been over-tightened during production. This can cause seizure of the crankshaft main bearing leading to abnormal noise and engine stalling.
kawasaki.remedy: Check crankshaft main bearing and retighten the crankcase fastening bolts.

kawasaki.defect: STRUT MAY BECOME LOOSE AND SEPARATE The front steering knuckle clamp bolts may not have been tightened sufficiently.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are affect (the vehicles that have had recall number RM/2005/030 completed prior to 03/03/2006) to inspect the steering knuckle clamp bolts and replace as necessary. Refit the clamp bolts and tighten to the correct torque.

kawasaki.defect: REAR BRAKE HOSE AND/OR REAR WHEEL ROTATION SENSOR LEAD MAY TOUCH REAR TYRE DUE TO INCORRECT ROUTING Due to incorrect routing the rear brake hose and / or the rear wheel rotation sensor lead may touch the rear tyre.
kawasaki.remedy: Inspect and re-route the hose and lead as needed replace the rear brake hose and / or sensor lead if they are damaged.

kawasaki.defect: THE OIL PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE MAY FAIL The oil pressure relief valve may fail resulting in low oil pressure.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the oil pressure relief valve.

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBILITY OF ENGINE STALL During extreme operating conditions high temperature or high humidity climates it is possible that the insulation on the spark plug cap may breakdown. This can result in either electrical leakage and a misfire. However in extreme cases this can cause the engine to stall.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall all affected machines and replace the spark plug.

kawasaki.defect: THE OIL PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE MAY FAIL The oil pressure relief valve may fail resulting in low oil pressure.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the oil pressure relief valve.

kawasaki.defect: THE FACTORY ECU PROGRAMMING MAY CAUSE THE ENGINE TO AFTER FIRE WHEN KAWASAKI QUICK SHIFTER IS USED UNDER HEAVY ENGINE LOAD The factory Electronic Control Unit programming may cause the engine to after fire when Kawasaki Quick Shifter is used under heavy engine load.
kawasaki.remedy: Reprogram the ECU. Replace the reed valves in the air suction valve assemblies on used motorcycles and if necessary replace any parts that have been heat damaged as a result of after-fire occurring.

kawasaki.defect: THE WIRING HARNESS FOR THE HORN MAY NOT BE DURABLE ENOUGH AND COULD BREAK The wiring harness for the horn may not be durable enough and could break.
kawasaki.remedy: Modify the wiring harness

kawasaki.defect: FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. This campaign includes some machines already actioned under recall RM95/2 which may have been fitted with incorrect chains at that time.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and replace the drive chain with a quality assured version.

kawasaki.defect: THE OIL PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE MAY FAIL The oil pressure relief valve may fail resulting in low oil pressure.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the oil pressure relief valve.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL It is possible for the regulator circuit board to get too hot which will lead to uncontrolled charging current output. This can cause discharge of the battery which may result in difficult starting or in some circumstances engine stall while riding creating the potential for an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines which are likely to be affected to replace the regulator.

kawasaki.defect: THE STEERING SHAFT MAY NOT HAVE BEEN CORRECTLY ALIGNED WITH THE STEERING GEAR The steering shaft may not have been correctly aligned with the steering gear during production.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the steering shaft and pinch bolt.

kawasaki.defect: SIDE CASE MAY BECOME DETACHED In certain circumstances it is possible for the side case latch pivot pin to break. This could result in the side case/s becoming detached from the machine.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the locks on both the left and right side cases.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY CUT OUT Electrical wiring may short circuit and cause the engine to cut out.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the likely to be affected machines and reposition the ignition switch block connector to prevent the harness from being worn or cut.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL AND/OR RUN UNSTABLY The wiring harness under the fuel tank may be damaged from contact with the frame edge. This can lead to a short circuit and the engine stalling. In addition on all 2011-2012 models and some 2013 models the throttle body holders may harden and crack in use due to insufficient heat resistance. This can lead to rough engine performance.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to inspect and where necessary repair the wiring loom. A guard will be fitted over the loom which may also have to be rerouted to prevent further contact. For applicable units the throttle body holders will also be replaced with improved ones.

kawasaki.defect: BRAKES MAY FAIL The left front brake hose may contact the brake disc during extremely heavy braking. This can damage the hose and lead to a fluid leak which could cause brake failure and result in an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to check and where necessary replace the left front brake hose and install a brake hose damper.

kawasaki.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL When the engine is cold it may stall when coasting under deceleration. This could increase the risk of an incident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and update the software in the Electronic Control Unit (ECU).

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBLE FUEL LEAK The overflow drainpipe inside the fuel tank may crack and leak fuel with a subsequent fire risk.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall affected machines and replace the fuel tank if the pipe is found to be cracked. Where the pipe is found to be serviceable a damper weight will be fitted to eliminate the vibration which may cause the pipe to crack. At the same time a new fuel level sensor will be fitted to address reports of inaccurate reading of the fuel gauge.

kawasaki.defect: Spark Plug Replacement The spark plugs may have been damaged during the manufacturing process. Continued use in this condition may result in unstable idle and in the worst case lead to the engine stalling.
kawasaki.remedy: To overcome this problem Kawasaki will replace the spark plugs.

kawasaki.defect: Spark Plug Replacement The spark plugs may have been damaged during the manufacturing process. Continued use in this condition may result in unstable idle and in the worst case lead to the engine stalling.
kawasaki.remedy: To overcome this problem Kawasaki will replace the spark plugs.

kawasaki.defect: DAL98 Clutch release shaft Welding Failure On affected motorcycles the clutch release shaft was not properly welded to the lever due to an improper manufacturing process.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the clutch release shaft.

kawasaki.defect: DAM 08 Retightening the Crankcase Fastening Bolts The crankcase fastening bolts may have been over-tightened during production. This can cause seizure of the crankshaft main bearing leading to abnormal noise and engine stalling.
kawasaki.remedy: Check crankshaft main bearing and retighten the crankcase fastening bolts.

kawasaki.defect: The plunger in the camshaft-chain tensioner can lock up during usage due to deterioration of internal parts The plunger in the camshaft-chain tensioner can lock up during usage due to deterioration of internal parts.
kawasaki.remedy: Replace the camshaft chain tensioner with a revised part.

kawasaki.defect: Replacement of the turn signal bulbs On eligible units of 2025 & 2026 W230 (BJ230A) and Meguro S1 (BJ230B) models the turn signal bulbs may fail prematurely due to an improper manufacturing process.
kawasaki.remedy: To overcome this problem Kawasaki has initiated a recall campaign to replace the front and rear turn signal bulbs.

kawasaki.defect: Replacement of the turn signal bulbs On eligible units of 2025 & 2026 W230 (BJ230A) and Meguro S1 (BJ230B) models the turn signal bulbs may fail prematurely due to an improper manufacturing process.
kawasaki.remedy: To overcome this problem Kawasaki has initiated a recall campaign to replace the front and rear turn signal bulbs.

kawasaki.defect: FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. This campaign includes some machines already actioned under recall RM95/2 which may have been fitted with incorrect chains at that time.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and replace the drive chain with a quality assured version.

kawasaki.defect: 1) FAILURE OF DRIVE CHAIN 2) STOWAGE OF TOOLS IN COMPARTMENT (ZX600-F1 MODEL ONLY) 1) As a result of incorrect heat treatment the drive chain may crack and ultimately fail. 2) Items or tools placed in the document/tool kit compartment may fall from the compartment into the drive chain area. (ZX600 - F1 model only).
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the affected machines and:- A) Replace the drive chain with a quality assured version. B) Replace the tool bag and mounting strap with modified versions and fit an additional cover (ZX600-F1 model only).

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBLILITY THAT AN INCORRECT O-RING HAS BEEN FITTED TO THE SHOCK ABSORBER On some eligible units the shock absorber may have been fitted with an incorrect O-ring. This can resulted in a hydraulic oil leak and create the potential for an accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Affected machines will be recalled at which time the shock absorber will be replaced with a quality assured item.

kawasaki.defect: MUFFLER MAY BECOME DETACHED The plug welds that secure the muffler bracket to the muffler body can crack allowing the muffler to become loose in the bracket. After continued use the muffler could separate from the main exhaust pipe creating the potential for an accident resulting in injury.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall affected machines to check the bracket welds and to add a damper or if necessary replacing the muffler.

kawasaki.defect: POTENTIAL LOSS OF STEERING CONTROL It has been identified thatthe steering tie rod ends could separate during operation due either to wear or impact leading to loss of steering control. Prior to each and every ride Kawasaki strongly recommends that you inspect the tie rods according to the inspection procedure. If free play is found the machine should not be ridden until such time as a repair has been carried out. If no free play is found the machine should not be ridden in adverse or rough conditions and or with a heavy load. Should you feel incapable of carrying out the inspection your Kawasaki dealer should be contacted for advice.
kawasaki.remedy: Recalled machines will have the steering tie rods replaced with quality assured parts.

kawasaki.defect: POSSIBILITY OF AN OIL LEAK. During cold starts the oil pressure relief valve may not respond quickly enough thus allowing excess pressure to build up causing the bottom of the oil filter to deform. This can cause oil to leak from the filter with the potential of a slip type accident.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall likely to be affected machines and fit a replacement oil filter.

kawasaki.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK Under certain conditions the fuel tank may crack at the front and rear mounting tabs. This can allow fuel to leak causing the risk of fire.
kawasaki.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and replace the fuel tank dampers and where necessary replace the fuel tank.
