webasto.defect: CERTAIN BURNER TUBES MAY NOT BE MANUFACTURED TO THE CORRECT SPECIFICATION The material composition of certain stainless steel burner tubes are not within the correct specification.  This can cause the burner tubes to deteriorate at an accelerated rate and can possibly fail.  In extreme cases this could cause a fire or allow exhaust fumes to enter the vehicle.  To date there have been no incidents of property damage or personal injury.
webasto.remedy: Webasto has initiated a recall of all 11 potentially affected units and will replace all affected burner tubes.

weightlifter.defect: POSSIBLE FAILURE OF KING PIN / BEDPLATE ASSEMBLY The possibility exists that the king pin rubbing plate might fail. Should this occur the semi -trailer could become detached from the drawing vehicle
weightlifter.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the rubbing plate modified/replaced as necessary.

westfield.defect: STEERING WHEEL RIVET CHANGE FROM ALUMINIUM TO STEEL Incorrect specification of steering wheel rivets.

FRONT WHEEL MAY LOCK The pad abutment plate securing screw may come loose. This can cause scoring of the brake disc surface face. If ignored it is thought possible the plate could stop the front wheel from turning and increase the risk of collision.
westfield.remedy: Recall the callipers that are likely to be affected. A new bolt with locking compound applied on assembly will be used.

westfield.defect: FUEL HOSE COULD PERISH OVER TIME Fuel hose may not be to correct specification.
westfield.remedy: Check and if necessary replace the affected fuel hose.

white.defect: TRAILERS ARE NON-COMPLIANT WITH REGULATIONS Trailers have been supplied without necessary type approval certification in place.
white.remedy: Trailers that do not comply must be presented for IVA and be tested accordingly.

wildax.defect: REAR SEATING SAFETY BELT INSTALLATION NEEDS A MINOR UPGRADE The rear seating safety belt installation may not perform as intended under high loads.
wildax.remedy: Depending on vehicle age an additional small bracket to the rear of the seat frame the replacement of some of the seat fixings and relocating of certain components within the seat box may be required.

winder.defect: TRAILERS HAVE BEEN SUPPLIED WITHOUT THE NECESSARY TYPE APPROVAL CERTIFICATION Trailers have been supplied without necessary type approval certification in place.
winder.remedy: Trailers must be presented for an IVA examination and be tested accordingly to gain the necessary approval certification.

winnebago.defect: TYRE PRESSURE INSTRUCTIONS ARE INCORRECT POSSIBILITY OF BLOW OUT It has been identified that the vehicle certification label may have stated the incorrect front tyre pressures.Should the vehicle be operated with incorrect tyre pressures over heating and a blow out may occur.
winnebago.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the certification label replaced with one which states the correct tyre pressures.

winnebago.defect: POWER STEERING MAY BE LOST It has been identified that the in- line power steering fluid filter can block due to failure of the filter screen to adhere to the housing resulting in a rise in return line pressure. In this situation the return hose can separate from the filter or steering gear fittingresulting in a sudden loss of power steering fluid and steering power assistance. Sudden loss of steering power assistance without warning could make the vehicle difficult to steer resulting in an accident.
winnebago.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the subject filters replaced with those of a larger capacity.

winnebago.defect: STEERING MAY FAIL It has been identified that the bolts which attach the steering arm to the steering shaft may have been under or over tightened. This can result in the bolts failing due to fatigue and loss of steering control.
winnebago.remedy: Recalled vehicles will have the steering arm bolts replaced and if necessary the steering arm.

witter.defect: INSUFFICIENT MOUNTING HOLE PRESENT There is a possibility that one mounting hole has been missed from the towbar side bracket.  Although there have not been any reported incidents it is possible that long term use may cause damage to the chassis which could result in a chassis failure.
witter.remedy: Recall all affected units and inspect unit.  If it is found that the side bracket does not have the correct number of mounting then the side bracket will be replaced with a new one.

woosung.defect: TYRE MAY BLOW OUT A manufacturing deficiency may result in sudden failure of the tyre body and rapid deflation which could impair the control of the vehicle.
woosung.remedy: Recall defective tyres and supply quality assured replacements.

workhorse.defect: BRAKING EFFICIENCY MAY BE AFFECTED The Actia instrument cluster the dash has been programmed with the incorrect software. This may result in the driver not receiving any warnings regarding defects within the vehicles brake system as the software will not illuminate warning lights indicating brake system fault codes. This could in extreme cases result a reduction in braking efficiency.
workhorse.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles and reprogram the Actia instrument cluster the dash.

workhorse.defect: FIRE MAY OCCUR On vehicles fitted with the General Motors L18 petrol/gasoline engine it is possible the retaining clip for the fuel rail pulse damper may not have been correctly heat treated. This could result in the retaining clip fracturing without warning which will not retain the damper and allow pressurised fuel to spray onto the engine. If an ignition source is present it may cause an engine bay fire.
workhorse.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles and replace the fuel rail damper retaining clip.

workhorse.defect: BRAKING EFFICIENCY MAY BE AFFECTED It is possible that the piston in the foot (Service) brake caliper (Bosch) may stick in the applied position.  If this occurs then it is possible that the front brakes may overheat which could cause the brake fluid to boil and result in reduced braking efficiency.
workhorse.remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the caliper with a new Bosch unit.

workhorse.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK On vehicles equipped with 75 or 100 gallon dual-fill fuel tanks the unused fuel-filler cap assembly was produced with a hose of the incorrect material. During normal usage the hose material may deteriorate which can result in a fuel leak. This can result in a risk of fire or depositing fuel onto the road surface.
workhorse.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles and replace the fuel-filler cap assembly.

wrightbus.defect: Tray Carrying HV Cables On Exterior Of Roof On Single Deck EV Products May Fail Tray Carrying HV Cables On Exterior Of Roof On Single Deck EV Products May Fail.
wrightbus.remedy: Extra support brackets added.

wrightbus.defect: LOSS OF CONTROL The control for the adjustment of the tilt and rake of the steering column is in a position where it could be accidentally operated by the driver  whilst the vehicle is in motion. This could cause an unexpected movement of the steering column and steering wheel.
wrightbus.remedy: On affected vehicles fit an interlock to prevent this.

wrightbus.defect: PARKING BRAKE CAN BE RELEASED BEFORE FULL AIR PRESSURE IS ACHIEVED The multi-circuit protection valve section of the Air Processing Unit (APU) has been incorrectly piped. The consequence is that the driver could release the park brake without sufficient pressure in the service brake circuits for them to function as the driver would expect. In this condition the red low pressure warning light for service brake circuits will either be independently illuminated or both together plus the low air pressure buzzer will be sounding.
wrightbus.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to change the position of two air pipes on the APU unit.

wrightbus.defect: SIGNS OF FATIGUE AT SOME OF THE WELDED JOINTS OF THE HYDROGEN GAS TANK SUPPORTING STEEL FRAME The steel frame supporting the hydrogen gas tanks in the �engine bay� of the vehicle may show signs of fatigue at some of the welded joints leading in some cases to the failure of the joint.
wrightbus.remedy: Do not drive and rework the various areas of the frame with redesigned and strengthened bracketry.

wrightbus.defect: ROOF PANEL DETACHED There is a possibility that the roof inspection door locks may loosen and allow the door to fall down whilst the vehicle is in service
wrightbus.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected fit modified locking plates and safety straps to lock to retain the roof inspection door safely in position.

wrightbus.defect: PARKING BRAKE CAN BE RELEASED BEFORE FULL AIR PRESSURE IS ACHIEVED The multi-circuit protection valve section of the Air Processing Unit (APU) has been incorrectly piped. The consequence is that the driver could release the park brake without sufficient pressure in the service brake circuits for them to function as the driver would expect. In this condition the red low pressure warning light for service brake circuits will either be independently illuminated or both together plus the low air pressure buzzer will be sounding.
wrightbus.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to change the position of two air pipes on the APU unit.

wrightbus.defect: DIRECTIONAL CONTROL MAY BE LOST Bolts (identified by CFL marking on head) connecting the lower wishbone assemblies to the vehicle chassis may be out of specification and at risk of failure. The failure of a single bolt is expected to have no adverse effect on the handling or integrity of the vehicle. A secondary failure mode on more than one bolt is likely to result in an unstable vehicle that will be difficult to control and will not handle in a normal way. The risk is that the driver could lose control of the vehicle.
wrightbus.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and where a lower wishbone assembly is found to besecured with bolts marked �CFL� the bolts will be replaced with a bolt manufactured by a different supplier. All eight bolts in the lower wishbone assemblies irrespective of the manufacturer of the originally fitted bolt will be replaced when one or more bolts with the �CFL� marking are replaced.

wrightbus.defect: REAR DOOR MAY OPEN WITHOUT WARNING It has been identified that the driver can inadvertently circumvent the correct operating procedure for the closing/opening of the rear plug and slide door. If the door operating sequence has been overridden then when the vehicle moves off from stationary the door can reopen a number of seconds after the vehicle has started to move off following the release of the park (halt) brake. Should this occur then the park (halt) brake will apply causing the vehicle to suddenly stop. The interlock will operate and the door will not reopen if the vehicle has exceeded 5 mph.
wrightbus.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to upgrade the Kibes software.

wrightbus.defect: VEHICLE MAY NOT BRAKE AS EXPECTED It is possible that the vehicle will not brake as expected and the driver may be required to brake harder as a result.
wrightbus.remedy: Update vehicle software.

wrightbus.defect: A hydrogen cylinder inner liner may fail on one of the five roof mounted tanks causing hydrogen gas to escape from the pressurised cylinder to atmosphere. A hydrogen cylinder inner liner may fail on one of the five roof mounted tanks causing hydrogen gas to escape from the pressurised cylinder to atmosphere.
wrightbus.remedy: The affected hydrogen tanks will be replaced with a revised variant.

In this condition the red low pressure warning light for service brake circuits will either be independently illuminated or both together plus the low air pressure buzzer will be sounding.
wrightbus.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to change the position of two air pipes on the APU unit.

wrightbus.defect: ENTRY DOOR CAN INADVERTENTLY BE OPENED AT SPEED Due to a software error in one of the vehicle's ECU's it is possible that if a passenger or occupant operates the front service door emergency controls (interior and exterior) when the vehicle is travelling in excess of 5km/hour then the front service door will function and open. This will only occur if the brake pedal is being pressed at the same time as the emergency control is operated. This could result in a passenger or occupant falling from the vehicle.
wrightbus.remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to update the software for the operation of the front service door.

wrightbus.defect: THERE IS A FOUL CONDITION BETWEEN BRAKE HOSE AND VEHICLE CHASSIS DUE TO FULL SUSPENSION TRAVEL Brake hose connection may crack and fail.
wrightbus.remedy: Replacement of the hose with an alternative designed component.

wrightbus.defect: ROOF PANEL MAY DISPLACE Interior roof panel may displace and fall to the floor
wrightbus.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and modify with modified scew fixings extrusions and brackets as necessary.

wrightbus.defect: THE HOSE SUPPLYING ADBLUE (UREA SOLUTION) TO THE DOSING SYSTEM MAY BE DEFECTIVE The hose supplying Adblue (urea solution) to the dosing system may be defective.
wrightbus.remedy: Replace Adblue hose with new higher specification hose.

wrightbus.defect: WIRING TO ELECTRICAL LOOMS MAY BECOME DAMAGED On Wrightbus StreetLite (Micro Hybrid) vehicles that are fitted with electric cooling pack fans it is  possible the electrical looms (cooling pack fan harness power cable and body harness looms) and the compressor delivery line hose may chafe on bodywork within the engine bay. This may affect the cooling fan operation and could lead to engine overheating or in extreme cases an outbreak of fire.
wrightbus.remedy: On affected vehicles check condition and routing of affected  looms. Where necessary repair and re-route looms according to manufacturer's instructions.

wrightbus.defect: POSSIBILITY THAT AN ARM MAY BECOME TRAPPED IN THE DOOR It is possible in certain circumstances for a person to trap their arm between the fully open door and a stanchion.
wrightbus.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and fit a partition in the gap between stantion and body that only allows a hand to grasp the stanchion.

wrightbus.defect: PSC-00004 Weaknesses identified in the exterior roof mounted hydrogen gas tanks support frame may lead to a failure of the frame during a vehicle impact.
wrightbus.remedy: Addition of structural beam and support brackets to the tank frame.

wrightbus.defect: Roof Mounted H2 Fuel Tank Support Bracket Bolts May Loosen Bolts in the brackets supporting the five roof mounted H2 tanks located at each end of each tank have the potential to loosen and drop out permitting movement of the bracket(s) and attached tank(s) with secondary movement in the associated system pipework. Under extreme braking conditions or if the vehicle is involved in a road traffic accident the roof tanks may become dislodged or become detached from the vehicle.
wrightbus.remedy: replacement of all bolts and nuts on the frame and frame attachment

wrightbus.defect: MAIN STARTER MOTOR LOOM MAY OVERHEAT Starter cables affected by heat from the turbo charger.
wrightbus.remedy: Re-route existing and replace damaged cables where evident.

wrightbus.defect: Alloy Rims May Crack Currently Wrightbus believe that there is a flaw in the wheel rim design contributing to the failure.

yamaha.defect: Leaking of GYTR racing fuel cap On affected motorcycles when the GYTR Racing Fuel Cap is installed there is a possibility that a small amount of gasoline leaks out of the fuel cap resulting in a risk of fire.

yamaha.defect: FUEL MAY LEAK It has been identified that the dimensions of the fitting bracket which secures the fuel tank to the frame are incorrect and this can cause the bracket to contact the fuel tank. This may result in engine vibration being resonance being transmitted to the fuel tank. This can cause the spot weld of the tank cover stay to fail which can cause due to transmitted through the stay. In the worst case fuel may leak.
yamaha.remedy: Recall all affected machine to change the fuel tank fitting bracket.

yamaha.defect: FRONT BRAKE PIPE MAY CRACK It is possible for a crack to develop inside the front flexible brake pipe. If a crack does develop a loss of braking efficiency will eventually occur.

yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and replace the Oil Delivery Pipe O-Ring.

yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace  the side stand bracket and to check and where necessary replace the wiring harness.

yamaha.defect: INCREASED RESISTANCE IN THE FRONT STOP SWITCH COULD CAUSE THE CRUISE CONTROL NOT TO WORK AND THE BRAKE LAMPS TO STAY ON On affected motorcycles increased resistance in the front stop switch could cause the cruise control not to work and brake lamps to stay on.
yamaha.remedy: Replace the stop switch with counter measure parts

yamaha.defect: REAR VIEW MIRROR MAY DETACH Under certain circumstances due to vibration a crack may develop at the rear view mirror pivot point and in extreme cases the mirror head(s) may become detached causing a safety issue primarily to other road users or bystanders.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the rear view mirrors with ones that have been modified.

yamaha.defect: THE STANDING ASSIST SYSTEM DOES NOT RELEASE IMMEDIATELY AFTER DE-ACTIVATION In some situations the standing assist system does not release immediately after de-activation.
yamaha.remedy: Do not use the Standing Assist function until the currently in-development modification has been installed.

This can result in the switch moving and could allow the machine to be ridden with the side stand in the lowered position. This creates an obvious danger hazard to the rider.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the affected machines and replace the mounting bolts with a new fixation kit.

yamaha.defect: TOP BOX FITTINGS MAY FAIL It has been established that if a top box is fitted to the machine this can cause stress on the rear mounting points of the frame which will eventually fail and result in detachment of the top box.
yamaha.remedy: Inform all owners not to fit a top box and once Yamaha have identified the fix recall all affected machines to have the rework completed.

yamaha.defect: THE ENGINE CONTROL UNIT CANNOT DETECT AN ERROR OF ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE SENSOR The engine control unit cannot detect an error of atmospheric pressure sensor.
yamaha.remedy: Affected units must have the engine control unit reprogrammed

yamaha.defect: THE PILLION SEAT FIXING BOLT MAY WORK LOOSE The pillion seat fixing bolt may work loose possibly resulting movement of the seat or in worst cases detachment of the seat.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and fit a revised method of attachment for the pillion seat.

yamaha.defect: THE REAR REFLECTOR DOES NOT MEET THE STANDARDS SPECIFIED BY UN-ECE FOR REFLECTION LUMINOSITY The rear reflector does not meet the standards specified by UN-ECE for reflection luminosity.
yamaha.remedy: The affected units should have the Rear Reflector replaced by countermeasure ones.

yamaha.defect: A COOLANT HOSE MAY FAIL DUE TO INCORRECT VULCANIZATION A coolant hose may fail due to incorrect vulcanization.
yamaha.remedy: Affected units must have the coolant hoses replaced with countermeasure parts.

yamaha.defect: THE 4 HANDLEBAR FIXING BOLTS MAY BE DEFORMED AND COULD BECOME LOOSE The 4 handlebar fixing bolts may be deformed and could become loose.
yamaha.remedy: Affected vehicles will have the 4 bolts of the handlebar holders replaced with new ones.

yamaha.defect: DRIVE MAY BE LOST The drive chain split link clip may crack and deform allowing the drive chain to come off with the subsequent loss of drive.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to replace the drive chain link with new remedial part.

yamaha.defect: VEHICLE MAY LOOSE STABILITY Under extremely bad and bumpy conditions coupled with relatively high road speed a potential defect with the steering under bracket stem (lower yoke) may cause it to crack and eventually break. If a break occurs the control of the machine will be adversely affected.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the affected machines and replace the steering under bracket stem (lower yoke) with a remedial part.

yamaha.defect: BRAKE PEDAL MAY FRACTURE On some units there is a possibility that the brake pedal has incorrect welding penetration between the arm and the foot support. In this condition the brake pedal may break when a breaking force is applied.
yamaha.remedy: On affected machines replace the brake pedal assembly with a modified assembly.

yamaha.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL The stator output may be insufficient to charge the battery which can lead to the speedometer not functioning and the engine may possibly stall and fail to restart.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and replace the stator.

yamaha.defect: THE REAR REFLECTOR DOES NOT MEET THE STANDARDS SPECIFIED BY UN-ECE FOR REFLECTION LUMINOSITY The rear reflector does not meet the standards specified by UN-ECE for reflection luminosity.
yamaha.remedy: The affected units should have the Rear Reflector replaced by countermeasure ones.

yamaha.defect: LOSS OF VEHICLE STABILITY The rear tyre may gradually deflate with an associated loss of vehicle stability due to poor sealing between the rear wheel and tyre.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and replace the rear wheel.

yamaha.defect: FRAME MAY CRACK It is a possibility that a small progressive crack may develop in the Frame which may result in instability.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines to fit a reinforcement bracket kit to the Frame

yamaha.defect: ENGINE MAY SEIZE In extreme cases the engine balance shaft drive gears could break and cause the engine to lock. This can lead to an elevated risk to the rider and other road users.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and fit new quality assured balance shaft drive gears.

yamaha.defect: DRIVE CHAIN GUARD FIXING BOLT TO SWING ARM  MAY LOOSEN The bolt fixing the drive chain guard to the swing arm may loosen due to vibration.
yamaha.remedy: Affected units must have the Collar & Bolt replaced with the countermeasure parts.

yamaha.defect: ENGINE MAY STALL The idle speed of the engine may become intermittently unstable. In rare cases this may result in the engine stalling when the machine is stationery or at low speed
yamaha.remedy: Recall affected machines and check Throttle Position Sensor.If necessary fit revised part.

yamaha.defect: POSSIBLE LOSS OF STEERING CONTROL Under certain circumstances there is a possibility that the excessive wear may occur within the tie rod end which in extreme cases may result in the joint failing and loss of steering control.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and replace the tie rod ends.

yamaha.defect: POSSIBILITY OF LOSS OF CONTROL The rear shock absorber piston rod nut may come loose. The shock absorber performance may be affected possibly causing a loss of machine control. The manufacturer recomends the machine is not ridden until the concern is assessed and where necessary repaired.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected and check if the machine is fitted with an affected shock absorber. Where an affected unit is fitted the complete shock absorber will be replaced.

yamaha.defect: BIKE MAY BECOME UNSTABLE The oil delivery pipe union bolt may be defective. As a result the transmission may be starved of oil causing damage and ultimately failure possibly resulting in a loss of control of the machine.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be defective and check the oil delivery pipe union bolt. If it is defective the engine unit will be replaced.

yamaha.defect: THE GEAR SHIFT MECHANISM TORSION SPRING COULD BREAK The gear shift mechanism torsion spring could break due to incorrect production process of the spring
yamaha.remedy: Affected units must have the torsion spring replaced with a countermeasure one.

yamaha.defect: SPEEDOMETER MAY MALFUNCTION Speedometer may malfunction and in extreme cases fail completely
yamaha.remedy: Replace the speedometer assembly with a new modified part.

yamaha.defect: ENGINE IDLE SPEED MAY NOT RETURN TO NORMAL Under certain circumstances a poor connection between APS and TPS may cause an incorrect signal to the ECU which in extreme cases may result in the engine idle speed not returning to the specified level even when the throttle is closed.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected to add a sub-lead to bypass the potentially poor connection.

yamaha.defect: POSSIBILITY OF ELECTRICAL FIRE The wiring connection joining the stator to the main wiring loom may become excessively hot and in extreme cases may cause other nearby components to ignite.
yamaha.remedy: Recall the machines that are likely to be affected to replace the stator to main wiring loom connector.

zenos.remedy: Recall the vehicles that are likely to be affected and check if the subject washers are fitted. Where necessary washers and a new nut will be fitted to the rear suspension.

zero.defect: BRAKE LIGHT MAY FAIL The brake lever travel range specification has been deemed to be too broad to ensure that the switch actuation point and corresponding brake-light activation will occur prior to moderate front brake application. This condition could lead to the brake-light not activating when moderate front braking is applied. Failure of the brake-light to activate when slowing down the motorcycle using moderate front braking may cause a hazard to drivers behind the motorcycle. This could lead to a possible crash and potential injury or death of the rider.
zero.remedy: Replacement of the front brake system brake-light switch with a switch manufactured to a revised actuation range that ensures brake-light activation prior to moderate front braking action.
